findings.excerpt: D.nVarpi (D.nMk (m, m')) = D.nMk (D.varpi m, D.varpi m') := rfl
findings.problem: This is the computation rule of `nVarpi` on the generator `nMk`, so it should be a canonical simp lemma. The sibling rule for `lambda` is `@[simp] lambda_nMk`, but this one has no simp attribute. It is only usable by explicit `rw`, and the file repeats `rw [QXA_nVarpi_nMk, ...]` in QXA_nVarpi_nVarpi (twice in one call), QXA_lambda_nVarpi, QXA_nMap_nVarpi (twice), QXA_IsCanonicalLMap_map_varpi and QXA_phi_nVarpi. The lemma is a private ad-hoc theorem in a downstream solution file, so other `simp` calls on `nVarpi (nMk (m, m'))` do not reduce it. The same gap applies to `nMap_nMk`, the analogous constructor rule for `nMap` in the definition file, which is also not simp and is also used through `rw`. The rewrite goes from a compound `nVarpi (nMk _)` to a single `nMk`, so termination is not a concern.
findings.proposed_change: Move `nVarpi_nMk` into Def_CerednikDrinfeld_GradedCartierNModule.lean, next to `nVarpi`, as `@[simp] theorem nVarpi_nMk ... := rfl`. Do the same for `nMap_nMk` (`@[simp]` with the same statement). Then replace the chains of `rw [QXA_nVarpi_nMk, lambda_nMk, lambda_nMk, ...]` with `simp [...]` or `simp only [nVarpi_nMk, lambda_nMk, nMap_nMk]`. If the definition file cannot be edited, at least tag the local lemma `@[simp]` (private is not an obstacle within the file).
findings.benefit: Readers get one canonical normal form for `nVarpi` applied to a generator, matching `lambda_nMk`. The several three-to-five-step rw chains collapse to a single simp call, and the rule is no longer repeated in each proof or rediscovered under a `QXA_` name in each solution file.

findings.excerpt: simp only [pow_zero, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, nsmul_eq_mul, Nat.cast_pow,
findings.problem: The same coercion-normalisation `simp only` list is hand-copied three times to prove `fun j => ((n • w j : ℤ_[p]) : ℚ_[p])`-style identities. It appears at line 203 (`Pi.smul_apply, nsmul_eq_mul, PadicInt.coe_mul, PadicInt.coe_natCast, smul_eq_mul`) and at lines 382 and 391 (`pow_zero, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, nsmul_eq_mul, Nat.cast_pow, PadicInt.coe_mul, PadicInt.coe_pow, PadicInt.coe_natCast, one_mul`). The goals compare the ℚ_[p]-scalar action on the coerced vector with the coercion of an ℕ-scalar multiple. There is no single lemma or simp set for this normal form, so each use needs a fragile hand-picked list. The second call also needs a trailing `ring`.
findings.proposed_change: Add one small lemma, for example one stating that the coercion `ℤ_[p] → ℚ_[p]` of `(n • w) j` equals `(n : ℚ_[p]) • (fun j => (w j : ℚ_[p])) j` for `n : ℕ`, or the function-level version. Tag it `@[simp]` only if it fits the existing coercion simp set. Otherwise name it and call it with `simp [lemma]` or `rw`. Then replace the three long `simp only` lists with that one lemma plus `pow_succ`/`ring`.
findings.benefit: The shared normal form is stated once and reused. The duplicated, order-sensitive lemma lists disappear, and any later change to the coercion simp set needs one edit instead of three.
